study type: Secondary data analysis of prospectively collected data
exposure: Mode of delivery (planned caesarean vs. urgent delivery)
outcome: Maternal outcomes (antenatal vaginal bleeding, gestational age at delivery, blood transfusion rates, major maternal morbidity, estimated blood loss)
Neonatal outcomes (birth weight, NICU admission rates, perinatal mortality)
cohort: 159 pregnant and postpartum women with confirmed placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) at Rafik Hariri University Hospital in Beirut, Lebanon between 2007 and 2020
finding: Urgent delivery among women with PAS is associated with worse maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to the planned approach.
gest_age: Median gestational age at delivery was significantly lower for the urgent group compared to the planned (34 vs. 36 weeks)
birth_weight: The urgent delivery group had a significantly lower birth weight (2177.5g vs. 2560g)
